author: OpenAI Codex, historical-assessments agent
changeNote: First complete 240-question assessment under the current 15 Values bank and scoring. Documented positions, user-authorised sound inferences and supported conditional neutral answers are distinguished. An independent evidence audit amended interpretation and source errors before archiving; substantive findings are recorded in review.notes. No 12Axes questions or scores were imported.

metadata.name: Ronald Reagan
metadata.description: US president associated with tax reductions, market-oriented reforms, military expansion and late Cold War arms negotiations.
metadata.scope: Personal positions and governing conduct during 1981–1989; earlier writings are contextual only. Historical analogies to contemporary technologies are explicitly inferred, not claims that the subject answered a modern questionnaire. Coalition constraints and contradictions are identified by axis.

axes.brief: Electoral legitimacy and constitutional separation of powers underpinned Reagan’s presidency.
axes.counterEvidence: Iran-Contra circumvention of congressional constraints qualifies accountability claims; it did not amount to a stated right to abolish elections.

answers.rationale: Competitive election establishes presidential legitimacy.
Rejected elite government detached from electorate.
Equal citizenship implies no educational voting qualification.
Constitutional legislation requires Congress, notwithstanding executive disputes.
Opposition parties remained legitimate electoral competitors.
Congressional scrutiny accepted institutionally despite secrecy failures.
Judicial review part of the constitutional order.
Union leadership cannot replace individual voters.
Government cannot exclude ordinary political opponents.
Representative government and state ballot democracy coexist; no categorical national repeal principle.
Presidential authority bounded by Congress and courts.
Constitutional impeachment fits accountable executive office.
No unilateral authority to suspend competitive tenure.
Local direct-democratic traditions balanced against fixed representative terms.
Government derives authority from consent of governed.
Civilian constitutional supremacy excludes autonomous military replacement.

axes.brief: Constitutional civil liberties coexisted with punitive drug policy and strong security enforcement.
axes.counterEvidence: Anti-government economic rhetoric is not a general libertarian position on drugs, policing or moral regulation.

answers.rationale: Drug prohibition rejects unrestricted self-regarding drug use.
Judicial approval makes serious-crime surveillance compatible with constitutional enforcement.
Peaceful assembly balanced against obstruction and public order.
Free institutional criticism central to constitutional liberty.
Individual responsibility balanced against protective public-health regulation.
Unsuspected long-term tracking raises constitutional privacy objections.
Road safety supports limited preventative sobriety enforcement.
Court finding supports preventive protection from serious harm.
Expression rights balanced against conservative obscenity restrictions.
Private communication normally need not entail universal government registration.
Credible serious violence supports geographically limited searches.
Strong public-order enforcement supports prohibition on credible disorder evidence.
Constitutional search protections generally require warrants.
Exposure of wrongdoing balanced against classified security obligations.
Self-defence firearm ownership fits his individual-rights orientation.
Indefinite unchecked detention conflicts with constitutional legal process.

axes.brief: Shared American citizenship and civic values accompanied a positive account of immigrant backgrounds.
axes.counterEvidence: Integration rhetoric and opposition to discrimination prevent equating cultural cohesion with compulsory abandonment of all identities.

answers.rationale: Common civic values prevail in direct conflicts.
Accommodation balanced against common institutions and costs.
Settlers expected to join American civic customs.
Nondiscriminatory American identity can retain foreign heritage.
Common language assists integration without eliminating accommodations.
Acknowledgement balanced with one inclusive national civic identity.
Established national traditions important to civic education.
Separate identities should not override common citizenship.
Shared civic calendar preferred with freedom for private observance.
Immigrant backgrounds can contribute to American national life.
Broad participation rather than insular separation strongly favoured.
Local practical accommodation balanced against integration.
Families should teach American allegiance alongside heritage.
Religious freedom balanced against generally applicable public rules.
Plural origins compatible with common American identity.
Civic integration prioritises shared values rather than enforced cultural erasure.

axes.brief: 1986 policy combined legalisation, enforcement and nondiscrimination rather than simple openness or blanket deportation.
axes.counterEvidence: Legalisation covered a defined established population; it did not authorise all future unlawful arrivals.

answers.rationale: Orderly controlled admission supports limits, not necessarily a rigid housing formula.
Welcomed lawful opportunity-seeking immigration.
Family and humanitarian routes contradict skills-only eligibility.
Family unity fits humane lawful immigration.
Humanitarian admission supported, bounded by orderly controls.
Amnesty for established residents balances stronger future enforcement.
Labour demand matters, but does not remove border controls.
Resource pressure balanced against immigrant economic contribution.
Family unity and numerical management require a conditional balance.
Legitimate employment supports lawful work entry.
Sponsorship fits orderly admission and responsibility.
Education alone not sufficient to waive immigration control.
Humane refugee exceptions compatible with orderly system.
Explicitly rejected discrimination among nations or peoples.
Lawful access balanced with self-support and welfare restraint.
Diverse origins welcomed but difference alone not an admission entitlement.

axes.brief: Military rebuilding and intervention combined with negotiated nuclear reductions.
axes.counterEvidence: Late arms-control diplomacy and preference for an all-volunteer military qualify maximal militarism.

answers.rationale: Grenada and proxy support extend beyond attack-response.
Diplomacy ultimately important alongside coercive pressure.
Military rebuilding accepted substantial fiscal costs.
Imminent threats justify preventative military action.
Intervention contradicted strictly defensive-only force.
Professional volunteer military preferable to general compulsory service.
Avoiding war mattered without accepting major strategic retreat.
Defence technology enthusiasm supports cautious military-effectiveness analogy. Historical analogy, not a recorded answer to this modern proposal.
Power projection central to global containment.
Ally defence excludes absolute non-intervention.
Global commitments require sustained overseas combat capability.
Negotiation preferred where possible, but force remained available.
Threat of force formed part of deterrence.
Negotiated risk reduction balanced with credible strength.
Cold War policy supports intelligence advantage.
INF-era arms reduction demonstrates acceptance of negotiated capability cuts.

axes.brief: Strong US sovereignty accompanied NATO commitments, international trade rules and selective cooperation.
axes.counterEvidence: Alliance obligations and arms agreements prevent treating sovereignty as complete unilateral isolation.

answers.rationale: US constitutional institutions retain ultimate authority.
External decisions require US consent rather than unconditional override.
Constitutional domestic authority generally prevails.
NATO and allied containment require lasting commitments.
Sovereign government can end commitments through domestic process.
External judicial control qualified by national consent.
National security can outweigh institutional objections.
Environmental cooperation acceptable, sweeping outside authority not automatic.

NATO cooperation supported agreed defence commitments, while US sovereignty retained independent foreign-policy choices. Membership of a bloc requiring a single common foreign policy therefore meets competing commitments.
Human-rights advocacy abroad does not confer external legislative supremacy.
Independent US monetary authority strongly preferred.
Shared problems can warrant allied resources.
Border authority remains a national responsibility.
Negotiated common trading rules advance open exchange.
US political sovereignty not ceded to federation.
Collective allied action can justify immediate national costs.

axes.brief: Private enterprise and contracting were preferred, with retained public programmes and strategic exceptions.
axes.counterEvidence: Medicare and Social Security funding are not evidence of government ownership of hospitals or businesses.

answers.rationale: Private enterprise should provide most production.
Utility regulation and private ownership generally preferred.
Explicit private-sector preference under equivalent performance.
Competitive industries normally left to private firms.
Private health providers compatible with public reimbursement.
Public strategic exceptions possible, but no general public rail principle.
Lower-cost comparable private delivery fits efficiency agenda.
Public finance instruments tolerated without a broad public-bank expansion aim.
Privatisation aligns with reducing federal business activity.
Housing assistance need not entail major public ownership.
Regulated private defence contractors fit security policy.
Private extraction normally preferred with public-resource conditions.
Contracting fits private-sector initiatives.
Security can justify retention, but regulation and private ownership preferred.
Repeated subsidies strengthen case for private restructuring.
Public broadcasting tolerated but private broadcasting generally preferred.

axes.brief: Free trade rhetoric and negotiated liberalisation coexisted with fair-trade retaliation and sector protection.
axes.counterEvidence: US import restrictions prevent assigning unconditional free-trade responses to reciprocity and strategic exceptions.

answers.rationale: General protection opposed, selected exceptions retained.
Strong defence of open international exchange.
National procurement interests balanced against price competition.
Firms should normally choose competitive suppliers.
Strategic supply exceptions qualify open import preference.
Fairness and reciprocal market access constrain unilateral concessions.
Temporary sector relief possible despite opposition to broad protection.
Foreign investment generally welcomed subject to security.
Farm interests balanced against expanding export markets.
Adjustment preferable to permanent protection.
Retaliatory measures accepted against unfair foreign barriers.
Nondiscriminatory taxation fits fair trade.
Subsidised unfair competition can justify remedies.
Tariff-cutting agreements advance global commerce.
Security screening may limit strategic foreign ownership.
Digital trade analogy favours cross-border consumer choice.

axes.brief: Market allocation, deregulation and private incentives prevailed over national production plans.
axes.counterEvidence: Defence procurement, retained minimum wages and central banking limit a pure laissez-faire reading.

answers.rationale: Production ordinarily chosen by firms.
Compulsory industrial targets conflict with market enterprise.
Supply-demand pricing preferred.
Selective priorities accepted, comprehensive investment plan rejected.
Consumer choice should guide business survival.
General price controls rejected, with exceptional protection possible.
Entry should be encouraged rather than justified by production need.
Credit normally market-allocated rather than industrial directives.
Capital freedom fits open private investment.
Subsidies exceptional rather than principal development method.
Dollar-based monetary stability retained, not general competing currency programme.

Reagan criticised employment effects of the minimum wage and proposed a lower youth rate, but retained a statutory floor. That combination supports neither abolition nor an unqualified wage-floor principle.
Private bargaining normally preferable, subject to legal limits.
Central-bank stability preferable to government production-plan control.
Market rents and supply incentives preferred.
Ordinary national production coordination conflicts with limited-government programme.

axes.brief: Tax reductions and limited welfare favoured retained earnings over substantial income equalisation.
axes.counterEvidence: Social Security preservation and targeted support prevent portraying a rejection of every safety net.

answers.rationale: Substantial income levelling opposed in favour of incentives.
Inequality alone does not justify higher tax burdens.
Minimum protection accepted, higher-tax expansion resisted.
Safety net rather than broad equalisation preferred.
Progressivity retained but top rates sharply reduced.
Tax cuts prioritised retaining earned income.
Large inheritance taxation viewed as limiting family accumulation.
Work and self-reliance support time and participation limits.
Broad wealth-transfer taxation conflicts with incentive programme.
Benefits restrained to reduce tax and dependency burdens.
Basic security balanced against benefits intended to match ordinary lifestyles.
Tax reductions were a defining priority.
Reagan proposed substantially increasing the special tax credit for low-paid workers. This directly supports income supplementation through the tax system despite his wider spending restraint.
His tax proposal retained graduated marginal rates, including a higher top bracket. Lowering the top rate does not establish support for eliminating higher marginal rates entirely.
Compensatory compulsory land redistribution conflicts with property rights.
Need-targeted support preferable to broad income supplement entitlement.

axes.brief: Civil constitutional government coexisted with public religious expression and voluntary school prayer.
axes.counterEvidence: Personal Christianity is not evidence for clerical veto or compulsory national confession.

answers.rationale: Secular constitutional reasons coexist with religious moral justification.

Religious morality informed his politics, but his voluntary-prayer amendment did not make religious teachings an official binding source of law. Civil constitutional institutions remained authoritative.
Religious leaders have no constitutional approval power.
Supported Judeo-Christian heritage, not a single established denomination.
Objective instruction balanced with voluntary faith expression.
His school-prayer amendment explicitly forbade compulsory participation. Voluntary prayer does not establish state religious instruction aimed at cultivating an officially recognised faith.
Civil laws bind state courts.
No clerical review chamber proposed.
Official prayer compatible with public religious recognition.
Voluntary religious participation supported, direct faith funding constrained.
Public religious symbols considered compatible with tradition.
Christian festivals accepted within public civic tradition.
Religious office alone confers no government seat.
Religious exemptions fit free-exercise orientation.
Civil marriage does not universally require religious consent.
Civil legal supremacy limits binding independent religious jurisdiction.

axes.brief: Presidency promoted family values, parental authority and opposition to abortion.
axes.counterEvidence: Divorce and women’s professional advancement qualify rigid traditional-role assumptions; contemporary gender questions are explicit analogies.

answers.rationale: Change should respect established family values.
Inherited moral traditions prioritised.
Alternative households not accorded identical preferred status.
Sex roles respected but women’s public careers accepted.
Traditional marriage framework opposed same-sex extension by inference.
Married family privileged in values rhetoric.
Presidential pro-life position opposes social acceptance of elective abortion.
Strong parental educational choice supports final say.
Conventional family ideal weighs against equal same-sex adoption.
Modesty consistent with inherited moral expectations.
Traditional usage preferred over compulsory identity-driven change.
Moral heritage deliberately transmitted through families and schools.
Professional opportunity balances traditional sex expectations.
Institutional continuity warrants gradual change.
Parents’ values constrain compulsory sexuality teaching.
Connection to inherited moral tradition is itself valued.

axes.brief: Technology, enterprise and biomedical research encouraged; protection of life and safety limited unrestricted experimentation.
axes.counterEvidence: Anti-regulatory views do not automatically settle invasive enhancement or irreversible ecological risk.

answers.rationale: Innovation benefits favour measured early adoption. Historical analogy, not a recorded answer to this modern proposal.
Research-only restrictions could unnecessarily delay useful innovation. Historical analogy, not a recorded answer to this modern proposal.
Development benefits can justify bounded habitat loss. Historical analogy, not a recorded answer to this modern proposal.
Medical benefit and safety testing require a conditional balance. Historical analogy, not a recorded answer to this modern proposal.
Productivity and retraining fit competitive technological progress. Historical analogy, not a recorded answer to this modern proposal.
Absolute habitat priority inconsistent with development orientation. Historical analogy, not a recorded answer to this modern proposal.
Food technology plausible under ordinary safety requirements. Historical analogy, not a recorded answer to this modern proposal.
Healthy enhancement balances personal autonomy against medical safety obligations. Historical analogy, not a recorded answer to this modern proposal.
Technical progress generally preferred to broad consumption restraint. Historical analogy, not a recorded answer to this modern proposal.
Major benefits balanced against credible environmental uncertainty. Historical analogy, not a recorded answer to this modern proposal.
Adult choice after basic safeguards fits limited-government inference. Historical analogy, not a recorded answer to this modern proposal.
Clinical reliability warrants supervised validation before broad diagnoses. Historical analogy, not a recorded answer to this modern proposal.
Protection of unborn life weighs strongly against enhancement experimentation. Historical analogy, not a recorded answer to this modern proposal.
Crop benefits balanced with demonstrable ecosystem safeguards. Historical analogy, not a recorded answer to this modern proposal.
Housing and transport supply generally warrant development. Historical analogy, not a recorded answer to this modern proposal.
Potential irreversible harm requires weighing severity against expected benefits. Historical analogy, not a recorded answer to this modern proposal.

axes.brief: New Federalism favoured state and local discretion within a permanent constitutional union.
axes.counterEvidence: Federal drug enforcement, defence and national rights show that decentralisation was not unlimited sovereignty.

answers.rationale: Protected state authority a defining federalist commitment.
National supremacy limited to constitutional competences.
Constitutional union not dissolvable by unilateral regional vote.
Federal programmes should not ordinarily erase legitimate state choice.
States retain constitutions within federal rights.
Decentralised policing preferable to a single national force.
Fiscal responsibility should move closer to states and localities.
Education administration explicitly favoured state and local control.
Subnational tax competition fits federalism.
National labour floors tolerated but regional flexibility preferred.
Local choice valued within state constitutional control.
State discretion and private choice qualify national coverage uniformity.
Local self-government fits decentralised principle within national rights.
Broad federal limits on tax competition generally resisted.
Regional stewardship appropriate for local effects.
Cross-state disaster coordination belongs legitimately to national government.

axes.brief: Family, moral education and opportunity were central explanations of character, alongside acknowledged individual talents.
axes.counterEvidence: This does not establish modern trait heritability estimates; mixed responses distinguish fixed individual differences from learnable conduct.

answers.rationale: Character formation through family and schooling favours upbringing.
Education-led national improvement weighs against inherited national IQ hierarchy.
Traditional sex differences balanced against individual opportunity and social formation.
Natural individual variation and formative experience both plausibly matter.
Educational opportunities develop and redirect interests.
Entrepreneurial talent and learned encouragement jointly shape risk-taking.
Community and family instruction cultivate cooperation.
Moral formation provides stronger explanation than inherited empathy alone.
School quality and disciplined study cultivate attention.
Moral heritage explicitly taught rather than biologically predetermined.
Guidance and knowledge can alter perceived threats.
Individual disposition acknowledged alongside learnable character.
Personal tastes and inherited dispositions not assigned a single dominant cause.
Opportunity and moral environment more central than racial biological criminality.
Self-discipline explicitly taught through family and education.
Individual productivity and barriers to opportunity both matter; no blanket gender-value account.

review.notes: Independently read all 240 questions and rationales, agreement directions, all axis briefs, counter-evidence and metadata. Checked presidential immigration, domestic-policy, prayer, tax and employment records. Corrected earned-income supplementation from neutral to agreement, separated lower top rates from a flat marginal-rate system, distinguished retention of a minimum wage from opposition to increases, and removed conflation of voluntary prayer with an official religious source of law or state faith instruction. Qualified NATO membership as evidence for a compulsory common foreign policy. Neutral responses reflect documented tensions in amnesty/enforcement, rights/public order and federalism, while contemporary technology and trait-causation responses remain explicitly modest interpretive inferences, not documented questionnaire responses. Portrait verification is separately performed during integration; similarity reviewed after all drafts are ready. Integration review by OpenAI Codex /root on 2026-10-04: portrait identity, local rendering, size and Commons attribution checked; the shared Image credits list includes this source. All 35 requested profiles were compared using calculated scores, with any resemblance at or above 95% explicitly reviewed against the named revision. Neutral-count warnings were retained only after the evidence review; they are not missing answers.
